answer: To raise a voting key, an agent must lock collateral and then obtain a cut-certificate: a short set of live payment channels that connect a public knoll of old keys to a socially distant mesa of keys, with no overlapping counterparties. The certificate and collateral remain in a haven vault until three later epochs confirm those channels actually settled. If the same operator opens a second key on a recycled channel set, the haven slashes the collateral. Cloning identities therefore requires new capital and a new, independently settled path.
